label: bad
seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken. I saw no score, band or tier of it or of its parent while building and labelling it; the parent's published verdicts in labelled-set.md §9 I did not open in this task.
claim: Black, moving second, wins by force (taking every white piece), in six of its own moves, and no win for either side can come sooner.
change: one: the setup is an ending, four white pawns (a4, c3, f4, h3) against Black's king, rook and knight on e8, h8 and b8.
aim: Four pawns against a rook and a knight look like a slow mop-up, and so they are for a player who sees the whole line; a player reading four plies takes pawns in the wrong order, lets one run to promote or stalemates the horde, so results should be mixed and games of ordinary length.

proof.text: A certificate (`certificates/horde-ending-with-a-rook-and-a-knight.json`): the tree opens with White's every first move, and at each of Black's turns gives Black's move, at each of White's lists every legal reply, ending each line in a position the engine calls won for Black (`rules.extinction`: White has no piece left), within six Black moves. `labelled/verify.py` walks it. Nothing sooner: Black has no forced win within five of its moves (`shortest`), and White, which loses by force, has no forced win at all. Found by `labelled/prove.py`'s search over the engine's legal moves.
